subject: hero-card-blast
label: The live castle Card-wright — mage-inspired card-firing stance and recoil, south-facing proof

runtimeCharacterAuthority.rule: This live PixelLab chibi is the only visual identity and proportion reference for the animation. Never use hero-cardwright/cardwright.png or any detailed portrait-register character as an animation reference.

identity.description: Athletic middle-aged Black man, a card-wright artisan, drawn as a big-headed chibi game character. Close-cropped black hair greying at the temples, short trimmed beard, warm dark brown skin, friendly readable face. Wears a slate-grey canvas work apron with brass tool loops over a deep teal rolled-sleeve tunic, dark work trousers, and a hard brass-cornered card case on his hip.
identity.avoid: no sword, no weapons, no shield, no brown leather adventurer gear, no armour, no wizard robe, no cape, no chosen-one insignia, no background, no floor, no fire, no flame, no fireball, no projectile, no glow, no magic effects, no extra cards, no camera movement

bibleNotes: Animate the exact PixelLab character used in the live castle under the hero-chibi asset key; identity, chibi proportions, costume, palette, and low top-down camera must not change.
THE CARD IS THE WEAPON AND HE IS NOT. He never punches, swings, or throws the card. His stance is a grounded casting brace: the body prepares for recoil while the power leaves the card.
The card is a temporary rigid prop for the body performance. Phaser renders the player's actual selected card over it.

NO FIRE IN THE SPRITE. The blast itself is a Phaser projectile spawned at the card. That is what lets one body performance serve every element in the game — fire, ice, void and the other 25 — instead of buying a clip per element.

palette.note: No scene palette reference. Player readability and identity continuity take priority, matching hero-card-slam.

poseReferenceNotes: PRIMARY AESTHETIC: use the clean, elegant limb placement of the selected PoseMy.Art mage spell-casting pose — a strong diagonal through the body, one casting arm reaching clearly into open space, an uncluttered chest silhouette, and the other arm providing visible counterbalance.

GROUND THAT ELEGANCE FOR RECOIL: keep one foot forward and one foot back, widen the base enough to read at 36x71, soften both knees, lower the hips slightly, and lean the torso toward the target before release. Do not copy the reference's narrow crossed feet.

Replace the spellcasting palm with one small rigid rectangular trading card held in the extended lead hand at chest-to-shoulder height. Let the support hand brace low on the presenting forearm near the elbow, not crowd the wrist or hide the card; preserve the long readable line of the casting arm.
The prepared pose leans forward. Only the release beat rocks the shoulders, hands, and card briefly backward and slightly upward as recoil; the planted feet do not slide.

Preserve an elegant asymmetrical silhouette at game scale: staggered feet form the base, the extended arm and card remain clearly separated from the face and chest, and the support arm reads as a distinct diagonal rather than merging into the torso.

animationNotes: SOUTH ONLY, ON PURPOSE. Animation is per-direction, so a clip exists only on the faces we pay for. This is the proof; approved, the other three extend from the same animation_group_id and charge only for the new directions.

ONE SHEET, TWO ENTRY POINTS. The draw and the present are one continuous clip so the frames connect, but the runtime can start partway in: the full sequence for the first shot from a card, and the presenting half for shots that follow while the same card is already in hand. That keeps the drama Raheem asked for without making repeat fire feel sluggish, and it costs no extra art. Record the frame index where the draw ends and the raise begins when the sheet is packed.

THE PROJECTILE MUST LEAVE THE CARD. The final presenting pose exists so Phaser has an unambiguous muzzle: the card's outer edge at arm's length. Record that offset from the feet anchor when packing — it replaces the estimated cardOrigin() forward offset in combat/blast.ts, which is currently a guess of 14 world units.

NO FIRE IN THE SPRITE, deliberately. Baking a fireball in would force one clip per element and lock the art to fire; as a Phaser projectile the same performance serves all 28 elements, and recolour handles their palettes for zero generations.
One continuous v3 clip rather than a chain, matching hero-card-slam: a chained generated start frame is where identity drift enters.

READS BY SILHOUETTE. He ships as a 36x71 frame at 71 world pixels tall. The staggered base, soft knees, forward brace, long lead-arm diagonal, separated support arm, and card isolated from the chest have to carry it; judge the packed sheet at 1:1, never zoomed in.

RUNTIME TIMING: the shot uses a 180ms windup, 30ms active beat, and 250ms recovery (ACTION_TIMING in combat/actionState.ts). Recovery retracts through frame 11 for 90ms, settles on frame 12, then spends the final 60ms blending into the current idle or walk direction.
NO AUTOMATIC PAID RETRY. Validate and present every direction before another generation is fired.

RAPID-FIRE CONTRACT: generation supplies entry, a long stable held stance, and exit. Phaser can keep the stance active between consecutive shots without replaying the draw from idle. Whole-body procedural recoil is intentionally disabled; any future recoil should come from approved character frames.
